updatedAt: "2026-11-09"

`apps/gateway` is a Cloudflare Worker routed on `tuturuuu.com/*`. It serves
anonymous public pages from the Workers Cache API and proxies everything else to
the Vercel production web deployment unchanged. It exists to cut Vercel
serverless and bandwidth cost for traffic that does not need a render.

The route `tuturuuu.com/*` is attached by the provider owner. Versions are
uploaded and deployed by the `gateway` job of `.github/workflows/web-opennext.yaml`
(see [Web route families](/build/devops/web-opennext-families#deploying)); more
specific routes (for example the roadmap Worker on
`tuturuuu.com/roadmap*`) keep winning over `tuturuuu.com/*`.

## Behavior

- **Manifest:** `apps/gateway/src/manifest.json` maps URL patterns to an origin
  and a cache class. `page` is an anonymous public page, `static` is a build or
  public asset, and anything unmatched is `bypass` (pure pass-through). A unit
  test checks that every path in
  `apps/web/src/lib/seo/public-routes.generated.json` is a `page` route, so the
  manifest cannot drift from the marketing pages.
- **Cache:** `GET` and `HEAD` on `page` and `static` routes. Fresh for 5 minutes,
  then served stale for up to 1 hour while a background refresh runs
  (`X-Gateway-Cache: HIT | STALE | MISS`). Only `200` responses without
  `Set-Cookie` and without `Vary: *` are stored. Pages vary by locale bucket
  (path prefix, then `NEXT_LOCALE`, then `Accept-Language`); `GET` and `HEAD`
  share an entry; tracking query parameters (`utm_*`, `fbclid`, `gclid`,
  `msclkid`) are not part of the key.
- **Bypass:** non-`GET`/`HEAD` methods, `Authorization`, `Range`, RSC requests
  (`RSC`, `Next-Router-*`, `Next-Action` headers or `_rsc` parameter) and, for
  pages, any session-like cookie (`sb-*`, names containing `session`, `auth` or
  `token`, `tuturuuu*`, `__Secure-`/`__Host-`). Static assets ignore cookies.
  Bypassed requests are forwarded with method, headers, body and cookies
  untouched; redirects are not followed and `Set-Cookie` is returned as sent.
- **Redirects:** a `Location` that points at the origin host is rewritten to
  `PUBLIC_HOST`, because the Next proxy builds absolute redirects from the
  request host. Marketing robots are finalized against the public ingress URL as described below.
- **Origin `Cache-Control`:** ignored on cacheable routes by default (dynamic
  Next pages send `private, no-store`). Set
  `GATEWAY_RESPECT_ORIGIN_CACHE_CONTROL=true` to honour `no-store` and
  `private`.
- **Failure:** missing `WEB_ORIGIN` returns `500`, an unreachable origin `502`,
  and a request that already passed through the gateway (`x-gateway-hop`) `508`.

## Configuration

| Name | Kind | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WEB_ORIGIN` | variable, set at deploy | Vercel production web origin, `https://<hostname>`. Must not be `tuturuuu.com` itself (that loops back). |
| `PUBLIC_HOST` | variable | Public hostname for redirect rewriting. Default `tuturuuu.com`. |
| `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX` | variable | `1` forces private robots, including cached pages. |
| `GATEWAY_MODE` | variable | `active` or `passthrough` (rollback flag). |
| `GATEWAY_RESPECT_ORIGIN_CACHE_CONTROL` | variable | `true` honours origin `no-store`/`private`. |
| `GATEWAY_WEB_FAMILIES` | variable | Comma-separated web family ids served by their `WEB_FAMILY_<ID>` binding. Default empty. |

No secrets are used. The Vercel origin hostname has to accept requests for its
own host; a custom origin hostname such as `origin.tuturuuu.com` must be added
as a domain on the Vercel web project before cutover.

## Cutover packet

Deploy (provider owner):

```bash
cd apps/gateway
bunx wrangler deploy --var WEB_ORIGIN:https://<vercel-web-hostname>
```

The route `tuturuuu.com/*` comes from `wrangler.jsonc`. Record the prior Vercel
production deployment id before the first deploy; Vercel keeps serving
`tuturuuu.com` unchanged until the route is attached.

Pre-flight smoke against the Worker with the route not yet attached is not
possible, so deploy first with `GATEWAY_MODE=passthrough`, verify, then switch:

```bash
node apps/gateway/scripts/gateway-smoke.mjs --base https://tuturuuu.com \
  --origin https://<vercel-web-hostname> --expect-mode passthrough
# after switching the variable to active:
node apps/gateway/scripts/gateway-smoke.mjs --base https://tuturuuu.com \
  --origin https://<vercel-web-hostname>
```

The smoke script checks 17 anonymous public URLs (`200`, second request served
from cache, no `Set-Cookie` on cacheable responses), the login page, that an
anonymous dashboard path redirects to login on the public host, that session
cookies and `Authorization` bypass the cache, and that `Set-Cookie` names match
the origin when `--origin` is given.

## Rollback

1. Fastest, keeps the Worker: set `GATEWAY_MODE=passthrough` (variable change,
   no code deploy). The Worker becomes a transparent proxy with no cache reads
   or writes.
2. Full removal: delete the `tuturuuu.com/*` route (or the Worker) in the
   Cloudflare dashboard. Traffic returns to the unchanged Vercel deployment.
3. No purge is needed: cache entries expire within 65 minutes and are
   never read in `passthrough` mode.

## Local checks

```bash
cd apps/gateway
vp test
vp lint --config .oxlintrc.json src --deny-warnings
```

## Marketing page groups

The gateway can serve a page group from the `apps/marketing` Worker instead of the Vercel web origin. Each group is one flag.

| Group | Paths |
| --- | --- |
| `legal` | `/privacy`, `/terms`, `/acceptable-use`, `/community-guidelines`, `/security`, `/legal/*`, `/security/*` |
| `company` | `/about`, `/branding`, `/careers`, `/contact`, `/contributors`, `/partners`, `/women-in-tech` |
| `products` | `/products`, `/products/*` except `/products/meet` and `/products/meet/*` |
| `solutions` | `/solutions/*` |
| `blog` | `/blog`, `/blog/*` |
| `home` | `/`, `/pricing` |

`/changelog`, `/download`, `/models`, `/meet`, `/meet-together`, `/portfolio`, `/qr-generator`, `/visualizations/*` and the Meet product page (`/products/meet`, `/products/meet/*`, which `/meet` redirects anonymous visitors to) always stay on the web origin.

Two Worker variables control the flip:

- `MARKETING_ORIGIN`: the `https://` origin of the marketing Worker. Without it, every group stays on web.
- `GATEWAY_MARKETING_GROUPS`: comma-separated group names served by the marketing origin, for example `legal,company`.

Flip a group by adding its name and redeploying the gateway variables. Roll it back by removing the name, or by clearing `GATEWAY_MARKETING_GROUPS`. Cached pages from the other origin are keyed separately and expire within the cache window, so a rollback is complete within one stale period.

Smoke for each group before the next one: anonymous 200 on two paths of the group, `x-gateway-cache` present, and `x-tuturuuu-runtime: native` on a cache MISS from the marketing origin.

`/assets/*` is the Vite build output of the marketing app. It always goes to `MARKETING_ORIGIN` (cached as static) and falls back to the web origin while `MARKETING_ORIGIN` is unset. It is not tied to a page-group flag, so rolling a group back does not move `/assets/*`; Vercel web has no `/assets` path.

## Marketing robots at the gateway

Marketing groups use the shared `seo-policy.json` Marketing allowlist against
`Request.url` at gateway ingress. Only canonical HTTPS `tuturuuu.com` URLs in
an enabled Marketing page group can be public. Private, unknown, malformed and
noncanonical Marketing responses remain noindex. Forwarded host/protocol
headers are not authority for this decision. Group ownership stays literal;
decoding a path for SEO does not move it to another origin.

Responses from Web and mounted apps keep their own robots policy on the
canonical `https://tuturuuu.com` URL: Web publishes `/changelog`, `/download`,
`/models`, `/portfolio`, `/cite` and `/products/meet` in its sitemap and marks
its private routes `noindex` itself. The gateway forces those responses private
only on a noncanonical URL or under gateway `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=1`, and strips
any `x-marketing-origin-robots` marker from them.

Marketing's response wrapper emits `x-marketing-origin-robots: 1` only when it
adds the standard private robots header for a noncanonical backend origin and
there is no upstream robots header or explicit `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=1`. The gateway
can remove exactly that origin-derived restriction on an eligible public page;
it consumes the marker on every response. Unmarked upstream noindex, including
explicit private directives, stays intact. Marketing remains private when
accessed directly. Bodies, status, CSP, Vary, authentication and cookie headers
continue through the existing response path.

Gateway `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=1` forces private robots even on cache hits. A backend
flag change cannot retroactively change an existing gateway cache entry: use the
gateway override when an immediate stop is required. Old unmarked cache entries
remain private until expiry or an independently authorized cache operation.

Regression coverage lives in `apps/gateway/src/marketing-robots.test.ts` and
`marketing-transport.test.ts`: rewritten backend requests, real loopback HTTP,
cache hits, redirects, explicit restrictions, and adversarial host/path inputs.
Source tests and policy fixtures do not qualify the full emitted Marketing
renderer. Before release, require exact-commit app build/type/lint/test/security
evidence, independent route/security review, emitted gateway and Marketing
Worker compatibility checks, and canonical/staging runtime header acceptance.
Provider deployment and cache operations belong to the release owner.

## Apps mounted at tuturuuu.com/&lt;app&gt;

An app moved from `<app>.tuturuuu.com` to `tuturuuu.com/<app>` gets two zone
routes on its own Worker: `tuturuuu.com/<app>` and `tuturuuu.com/<app>/*`. They
are more specific than the gateway's `tuturuuu.com/*`, so those requests never
reach the gateway. One case slips through: a zone route cannot match the bare
path once a query string is present, so `tuturuuu.com/<app>?x=1` would fall to
the gateway and on to Web.

For that case the gateway hands `/<app>` (any query) to the app's Worker
through a service binding. An app that serves its nested paths through the
gateway instead of its own `/<app>/*` zone route opts in explicitly:

- Add the exact mount to `GATEWAY_MOUNTED_PATHS` (comma-separated, e.g.
  `/learn,/tasks`). Add `/<app>/*` (e.g. `/learn,/learn/*`) only when the
  gateway should also hand that app its nested paths.
- Bind the app Worker as `MOUNT_<SEGMENT>` (`MOUNT_LEARN`, `MOUNT_STORE`).

A service binding is not a same-zone subrequest, so the request reaches the
Worker, not the Vercel origin. Only requests on `PUBLIC_HOST` mount, and
`/api` never mounts. The URL, prefix, query, method and body reach the app
unchanged. Client-supplied forwarding and framework-internal headers
(`x-forwarded-*`, `Forwarded`, `x-real-ip`, `x-original-*`, `x-rewrite-url`,
`x-middleware-*`, `x-nextjs-*`, `x-next-intl-*`, `x-tuturuuu-*`, `x-gateway-*`)
are stripped and none are synthesized, so a mounted app takes its public origin
from its own configuration. Responses carry `x-gateway-cache: MOUNT` and are
never cached by the gateway. Nested paths without a `/<app>/*` entry,
lookalikes (`/learning`), other hosts and unlisted or unbound paths keep going
to `WEB_ORIGIN`. Regression coverage lives in
`apps/gateway/src/worker-mount.test.ts`.

**Rollback for one app:** remove its two zone routes and its
`GATEWAY_MOUNTED_PATHS` entries. Its subdomain serves again. Mount dispatch
precedes `GATEWAY_MODE`, so `passthrough` alone does not roll back a mount.

## Web route families

Route families of `apps/web` built as their own Worker (see
[Web route families on Cloudflare](/build/devops/web-opennext-families)) are
reached through gateway service bindings on the existing `tuturuuu.com/*`
route. Family Workers have no routes, so no zone or DNS change is involved.

- `webFamilies` in `apps/gateway/src/manifest.json` lists each family: `id`,
  `binding` (`WEB_FAMILY_<ID>`), `exact` paths, raw `prefix` entries (each
  ending in `/`), `exclude` subtrees, `localized` and `assetPrefix` (`/_f/<id>`
  for page families, stripped before the family sees the request). Matching is
  method-agnostic.
- `webFamilies.deny` lists subtrees that never reach a family, whatever the
  flags say: `/api/v1/auth/accounts`, `/api/cron`,
  `/api/notifications/send-immediate`, `/api/v1/infrastructure`,
  `/api/v1/devboxes`, the ChatGPT file-store routes and `/_next/image`.
- `GATEWAY_WEB_FAMILIES` (comma-separated ids, default empty) turns families
  on. A listed family serves its paths only when its binding exists;
  otherwise they stay on `WEB_ORIGIN`. Percent-encoded, doubled-slash and
  non-`PUBLIC_HOST` requests always stay on `WEB_ORIGIN`.

Order in the handler: loop check, mounts, then (unless `GATEWAY_MODE` is
`passthrough`) deny list and the first flagged, bound family, then the cached
manifest path. Families do not apply the signed-in/RSC/server-action bypass:
those requests are what moves.

The family request keeps method, body, query, cookies, `authorization` and
`cf-connecting-ip`. Client forwarding headers (the list in the mounted-app
section) are stripped, and the gateway sets `x-forwarded-host: PUBLIC_HOST`,
`x-forwarded-proto: https` and `x-gateway-hop: 1`. Next's server-action origin
check relies on this contract. Responses carry `x-gateway-cache: FAMILY` and
`x-gateway-family: <id>`, are never stored in the gateway cache, and keep
`Set-Cookie` and `cache-control` as the family sent them. A throwing binding
answers `502 gateway family unreachable`.

Security header parity: the gateway fills `Strict-Transport-Security:
max-age=63072000` and `Referrer-Policy: same-origin` on family responses that
lack them, matching the live Vercel responses. It never overrides a header the
family sends (CSP, `X-Frame-Options`, route-specific `Referrer-Policy`) and
adds no `Permissions-Policy`, which the live responses do not carry. The other
live security headers (`X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-XSS-Protection`,
`Expect-CT`, `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`) match the zone's "Add security
headers" managed transform and appear on every gateway response today; the
per-family S3 header diff confirms them on family responses. Regression coverage
lives in `apps/gateway/src/web-family.test.ts`.

**Rollback for one family:** remove its id from `GATEWAY_WEB_FAMILIES`.
**All families:** `GATEWAY_MODE=passthrough`. Enabling a family is a change of the
`GATEWAY_WEB_FAMILIES` repository variable followed by a run of the gateway job,
which adds the family's service binding.

## Path ownership and rollback

Each gateway path has one owner. Alias collisions are rejected at manifest
validation. A one-action rollback restores all affected surfaces, including
bare-query fallback paths. Mounted app traffic bypasses the gateway cache and
forwarding headers are stripped.
